recipes.title: Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.description: Fluffy American breakfast pancakes spiced with cinnamon and nutmeg, with blueberries folded into the batter.

steps.instructionText: Sift together the flour, sugar, baking powder, cream of tartar, salt, cinnamon and nutmeg. Set aside.
Whisk the buttermilk, melted butter, vanilla and egg yolks in a large bowl. Mix in the flour mixture, then the blueberries.
Whip the egg whites until stiff but not dry, then fold them into the batter.
Heat a large pan or griddle over medium heat and brush lightly with oil.
Ladle in 1/4 cup of batter for each pancake and cook until set and bubbly on top.
Flip each pancake and cook for 1 more minute. Serve warm with your favourite topping.

recipes.title: Chocolate Chip Pancakes
recipes.description: Thick, tender American pancakes studded with semisweet chocolate chips and cooked in butter.

steps.instructionText: Warm the butter and milk together in a small saucepan over low heat until the butter melts. Let it cool slightly and stir in the vanilla.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs in a large bowl, then whisk in the milk mixture.
Add the dry ingredients and mix just until barely blended. Stir in the chocolate chips.
Heat a griddle or large skillet over medium heat. Melt a little butter until bubbly.
Ladle 3 tablespoons of batter per pancake onto the pan. Cook until bubbly on top and golden underneath.
Flip and cook for 30 seconds more until golden. Repeat with the rest of the batter and serve hot.

recipes.title: Light and Fluffy Pancakes
recipes.description: Small, airy buttermilk pancakes with vanilla, cooked on a lightly oiled griddle until golden.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil, for brushing the pan

steps.instructionText: Start heating a large non-stick skillet or griddle over low heat.
Mix the flour, sugar, salt, baking powder and baking soda in a bowl.
Warm the buttermilk and milk until they are at room temperature, then whisk in the egg, melted butter and vanilla.
Whisk the wet ingredients into the dry until just mixed. Add 1-2 tsp water if needed for a thick but pourable batter.
Raise the heat to medium and brush the pan generously with oil.
Ladle in about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake, in batches. Cook until the bottoms are golden and the tops bubble, 2-3 minutes.
Flip and cook until golden on the other side. Brush the pan with oil between batches and serve hot.

recipes.title: Whole Wheat Pancakes
recipes.description: Wholesome griddle pancakes made with whole wheat flour, milk and a little oil.

steps.instructionText: Mix the whole wheat flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, beat the egg, then stir in the milk and the 2 tbsp oil.
Mix the wet and dry ingredients just enough to remove dry spots and no more.
Heat a frying pan over medium heat and grease it with oil. It is hot enough when a drop of water dances on it.
Pour about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake and spread to about 10 cm across.
When the bubbling settles and the edges look slightly dry, flip the pancake.
Cook until golden, then remove and repeat with the remaining batter.

recipes.title: Oven Pancake
recipes.description: Eggless American pancake batter poured into a hot skillet and baked in one thick golden round.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 230 °C (450 °F) and oil an 8-inch (20 cm) oven-safe skillet.
Combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and sugar in a bowl.
Add the milk, vegetable oil and vanilla and stir well.
Stir in the apple cider vinegar, mix well and pour immediately into the skillet.
Bake for 18-20 minutes, then serve.

recipes.title: Banana Nut Muffins
recipes.description: Wholesome whole wheat muffins with mashed banana and chopped walnuts, from a Joy of Cooking style recipe.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and grease a muffin tin.
Beat together the eggs, honey, milk, vegetable oil and mashed bananas.
Combine the white flour, whole wheat flour, salt, baking powder and walnuts.
Mix the dry ingredients gently into the wet. A lumpy batter is normal.
Spoon the batter into the muffin tin and bake for 20-25 minutes.
Cool before serving.

recipes.title: Bran Muffins
recipes.description: Quick buttermilk muffins made with wheat bran and brown sugar, a good fibre-rich breakfast.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and grease or line a muffin tin.
Stir the wheat bran and buttermilk together in a mixing bowl.
Cream the egg, brown sugar and margarine together in another bowl.
Combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a third bowl.
Mix the creamed mixture into the bran mixture, add the flour mixture and stir just to moisten.
Fill the muffin cups 3/4 full and bake for 15-20 minutes.

recipes.title: Oatmeal Muffins
recipes.description: Soft buttermilk muffins made with rolled oats, brown sugar and coconut.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and grease or line a muffin tin.
Stir the rolled oats and buttermilk together in a mixing bowl.
In another bowl, combine the flour, coconut, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Make a well in the centre.
Add the egg and melted margarine to the oat mixture and mix well.
Pour it all at once into the flour mixture and stir just to moisten.
Fill the muffin cups 3/4 full and bake for 15-20 minutes.

recipes.title: Lemon Poppy Seed Muffins
recipes.description: Light lemon-yogurt muffins speckled with poppy seeds and topped with a sweet lemon glaze.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and grease a 12-cup muffin tin.
Sift the flour, sugar, poppy seeds, lemon zest, lemon extract, baking powder, baking soda and salt into a bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix the milk, vegetable oil, lemon yogurt and egg.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture in three steps, taking care not to over-mix.
Divide the batter between the muffin cups and bake for 16 minutes, until golden and springy.
Meanwhile, stir the confectioners' sugar with the lemon juice until smooth to make the glaze.
Drizzle the muffins with the glaze. Cool on a rack for 10 minutes, then remove from the tin.

recipes.title: Zucchini Bread
recipes.description: Sweet, moist spiced quick bread made with grated zucchini (courgette); makes two loaves.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F). Grease and flour two 8 x 4-inch loaf pans.
Sift together the flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda and cinnamon.
Beat the eggs, vegetable oil, vanilla and sugar together in a large bowl.
Add the sifted ingredients and beat well. Stir in the zucchini until combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared pans.
Bake for 40 minutes to 1 hour, until a tester inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cool in the pans for 20 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Cookies
recipes.description: Classic crisp-edged American cookies made with peanut butter, brown sugar and butter, flattened with a fork.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).
Cream together the white sugar, brown sugar, melted butter, egg and vanilla until smooth.
Mix in the flour, peanut butter, salt and baking soda to make a dough.
Flatten small pieces of dough with a fork on an ungreased baking sheet, at least 5 cm apart.
Bake for 8-10 minutes, until golden brown.
Let the cookies cool.

recipes.title: Snickerdoodles
recipes.description: Soft butter cookies with a tangy cream of tartar bite, rolled in cinnamon sugar before baking.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 205 °C (400 °F).
Mix the flour, salt, baking soda, cream of tartar, white sugar, shortening, butter and eggs into a dough.
Roll the dough into balls of about 1 tbsp each.
Mix the 2 tbsp sugar with the cinnamon and roll the balls in it.
Bake for 10 minutes, until crisp and light brown.
Sprinkle the hot cookies generously with more cinnamon.

recipes.title: Soft Sugar Cookies
recipes.description: Old-fashioned soft sugar cookies, shaped into balls and baked until set; a century-old Ontario family recipe.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F).
Lightly beat the eggs to break the yolks, then mix in the shortening until loose. Soften butter slightly first if using it.
Mix in the sugar, vanilla and salt.
Add the baking powder, then slowly add the flour until the dough can be shaped without sticking too much to your hands.
Shape into balls and place on a greased or parchment-lined pan.
Bake for 15-20 minutes.

recipes.title: Chewy Ginger Cookies
recipes.description: Soft, chewy molasses-and-ginger cookies rolled in sugar, baked until just cracked on top.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F) and grease a cookie sheet.
Cream the butter and brown sugar with a mixer.
Beat in the egg and stir in the molasses.
Combine the baking soda, flour, cinnamon, ginger, cloves and salt in a separate bowl, then gently mix into the wet mixture to make a dough.
Shape into 2.5 cm balls and roll them in sugar. Do not flatten them.
Place on the cookie sheet about 4-5 cm apart and bake for about 11 minutes, until cracked but still soft inside.
Cool to room temperature.

recipes.title: Molasses Cookies
recipes.description: Old-time soft spiced cookies sweetened with molasses, made as drop or rolled cookies with sour milk.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and grease or line cookie sheets.
Combine the vinegar with the milk and set aside to sour.
Mix the baking soda, cinnamon, ginger and 2 1/2 cups of the flour.
Cream the sugar and shortening, then beat in the molasses and egg until smooth.
Alternately mix in the dry mixture and the soured milk, starting and ending with the dry mixture.
Mix in more flour bit by bit for a soft dough, then chill the batter for at least 1 hour.
Scoop onto the sheet, flatten with a sugared glass and press walnuts or raisins on top. Or roll out and cut shapes.
Bake for 8-10 minutes.

recipes.title: Triple Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.description: Cocoa cookies loaded with white and milk chocolate chips, chewy if baked a little less.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, plus extra for greasing

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Grease 3 baking trays.
Mix the flour, cocoa, bicarbonate of soda and salt in a bowl.
Beat the butter and sugar until soft and fluffy, then beat in the egg.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients, then fold in the white and milk chocolate chips.
Spoon heaped tablespoons of dough onto the trays, well spaced apart.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or 10 minutes for a chewier cookie.
Move the cookies to wire racks to cool.

recipes.title: Hermits (Spice Bar Cookies)
recipes.description: Chewy New England molasses spice cookies with raisins, baked as strips and cut into bars.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Stir together the flour, raisins, brown sugar, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, baking powder and salt, breaking up any sugar lumps.
Stir in the molasses, melted butter, vanilla and egg until fully combined.
Shape the dough into two strips on the pan, well apart from each other.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, until a toothpick in the centre of the strips comes out dry.
Cool slightly, then slide the strips on their parchment to a rack to cool completely.
Cut the strips into wide bars and scrape them off the parchment. Enjoy with milk or tea.

recipes.title: Pecan Blondies
recipes.description: Chewy brown-sugar bar cookies, like brownies without chocolate, full of toasted pecans.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 170 °C (325 °F) and butter an 8 x 8-inch (20 cm) baking dish.
Toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium-high heat, stirring often, until fragrant and slightly coloured.
Stir the flour, baking powder and salt together in a small bowl.
Stir the melted butter, brown sugar and vanilla until uniform, breaking up any lumps. Beat in the egg until creamy.
Gently fold in the flour mixture, then the toasted pecans. Do not overmix.
Spread the batter into the dish and bake for 30 minutes, or to your preferred doneness.
Let cool, then cut into bars.

recipes.title: Fudge Crackle Cookies
recipes.description: Brownie-like chocolate cookies made in a saucepan, with a cracked, sugar-dusted dome and walnuts.

steps.instructionText: Combine the flour, baking powder and salt.
Melt the margarine and chocolate together in a large saucepan over low heat, then take it off the heat.
Mix the eggs, sugar, vanilla and walnuts into the chocolate mixture.
Mix in the flour mixture. Cover and refrigerate until firm, ideally overnight.
Preheat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F). Roll the dough into 4 cm balls, coat them in coarse sugar and place on a cool, ungreased cookie sheet with room to spread.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Remove the cookies from the sheet immediately, or they will stick firmly.

recipes.title: Chocolate Crinkles
recipes.description: Fudgy chocolate cookies rolled in icing sugar so they crack into a black-and-white pattern as they bake.

steps.instructionText: Mix the vegetable oil, melted chocolate and sugar.
Blend in the eggs one at a time until well mixed, then add the vanilla.
Stir in the flour, baking powder and salt.
Chill the dough for several hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F).
Drop teaspoonfuls of dough into the confectioners' sugar, roll into balls and coat well.
Place the balls about 5 cm apart on a greased baking sheet and bake for 10-12 minutes.

recipes.title: Date Bars
recipes.description: Oat crumble bars with a cooked date filling between a buttery brown-sugar base and topping.

steps.instructionText: Mix the dates, sugar and water in a saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, for about 10 minutes until thickened. Let it cool.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and grease a 13 x 9-inch pan.
Cream the butter, shortening and brown sugar together.
Mix in the flour, salt, baking soda and oats to make a crumble.
Press half the crumble evenly into the bottom of the pan and spread the date filling on top.
Cover with the remaining crumble, pressing lightly.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, until light brown. Cut into bars while warm.

recipes.title: Gingerbread Cake
recipes.description: Soft, dark spiced golden-syrup cake in the English style, best left a day before cutting.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 170 °C (325 °F) and grease an 8-inch (20 cm) square cake tin.
Heat the butter, brown sugar and golden syrup gently in a saucepan until the butter melts.
Put the flour, baking powder, mixed spice and ground ginger in a bowl. Pour in the melted butter mixture and beat thoroughly.
Warm the milk in a saucepan, add it to the bowl and beat thoroughly.
Beat the eggs and stir them into the mixture. Pour into the tin.
Bake for 1 hour.
Cool in the tin for 15 minutes, then turn out. Leave for at least 1 day before cutting into squares.

recipes.title: Applesauce Cake
recipes.description: Old-fashioned spiced raisin cake with almonds and unsweetened applesauce, baked in two round pans.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Grease and line two round cake pans.
Cream the butter and sugar in a bowl until light and fluffy.
Mix in the raisins, flour, cloves, allspice, cinnamon, ground almonds and applesauce.
Dissolve the baking soda in the hot water and stir it into the batter.
Pour the batter into the pans and bake for 45 minutes, until golden.
Move the cakes to a wire rack to cool.

recipes.title: Apple Cake
recipes.description: Simple spiced butter cake with chopped apples, served warm with whipped cream.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F). Grease and line a cake pan.
Cream the butter and sugar together until fluffy, then beat in the eggs.
Sift the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and nutmeg together and mix into the batter until just combined.
Fold in the apples and transfer the batter to the pan.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Serve warm with whipped cream.

recipes.title: Carrot Cake
recipes.description: Moist spiced carrot and walnut cake topped with a cream cheese frosting.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F) and grease a 26 cm cake tin.
Mix the vegetable oil, flour, bicarbonate of soda, sugar, eggs, salt, cinnamon, carrots and walnuts in a food processor for 5 minutes.
Pour the batter into the tin and bake for 45 minutes.
Check the cake is cooked, then cool in the tin for 10 minutes.
Unmould the cake onto a cooling rack and let it cool completely.
For the topping, cream the cream cheese, topping sugar and butter in a bowl until smooth and soft.
Spread the frosting over the cake with a palette knife.

recipes.title: Rhubarb Cake
recipes.description: Tender buttermilk cake studded with tangy rhubarb and finished with a cinnamon-sugar crust.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F) and grease a 9 x 13-inch pan.
Cream the brown sugar and butter until fluffy, then beat in the egg and salt.
Stir in the buttermilk, baking soda, vanilla and flour. Add the rhubarb and stir until mixed in.
Pour the batter into the pan.
Combine the 1/4 cup sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over the batter.
Bake for 30-35 minutes.

recipes.title: Wacky Cake (Eggless Chocolate)
recipes.description: Depression-era chocolate cake with no eggs or butter, mixed in one bowl with oil and vinegar.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F) and grease a square cake pan.
Combine the flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
Add the water, vegetable oil, vinegar and vanilla and blend thoroughly.
Pour the batter into the pan and bake for 35-40 minutes.
Cool completely before serving.

recipes.title: Traditional Pound Cake
recipes.description: Classic English pound cake made with equal weights of flour, butter, sugar and eggs.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F) and grease and flour a baking pan.
Cream the butter and caster sugar together until fluffy.
Beat in the eggs and the vanilla extract.
Gradually sift in the self-raising flour. Fold in the dried fruit if using.
Transfer to the pan and bake for 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out with no moist crumbs.

recipes.title: Flourless Chocolate Cake
recipes.description: Dense, rich chocolate cake of chocolate, butter, eggs and sugar, baked in a water bath and chilled.

steps.instructionText: Melt the chocolate and butter in a bowl set over a pan of simmering water. Whisk lightly until smooth, then cool, stirring.
Preheat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F).
Beat the eggs and sugar until creamy, then gradually mix in the melted chocolate.
Pour into a baking tin or 8 individual moulds. Cover with aluminium foil and set in a deeper baking tray.
Pour boiling water into the tray to half the height of the moulds.
Bake for about 30 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool at room temperature, then chill in the fridge for about 10 hours.
Remove from the mould, place on a plate and garnish.

recipes.title: Hot Milk Cake
recipes.description: Old-fashioned two-layer vanilla sponge made by beating eggs well and folding in hot milk and butter.

steps.instructionText: Take the eggs and butter out of the fridge an hour before baking. Preheat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F).
Heat the milk and butter together until the butter melts. Cool until just warm, then add the vanilla.
Combine the cake flour, baking powder and salt.
Whip the eggs in a large bowl until light and lemon-coloured, which can take 5-10 minutes.
Add the sugar slowly, beating well, then add the dry ingredients.
Add the milk mixture very slowly, folding it in by hand toward the end.
Divide the batter between two greased and floured 9-inch (23 cm) round pans and bake for about 30 minutes.
Cool on racks for 10 minutes, then turn out to cool completely. Frost or serve with strawberries.

recipes.title: Banana Cream Pie
recipes.description: Pastry shell layered with sliced bananas and a vanilla custard cream, cooled until set.

steps.instructionText: Combine the sugar, flour and salt in a saucepan.
Add the milk gradually.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until bubbly. Cook and stir for 2 more minutes, then remove from the heat.
Stir a small amount of the hot mixture into the egg yolks, then stir the yolks into the hot mixture.
Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, then remove from the heat.
Add the butter and vanilla and stir until smooth.
Arrange the sliced bananas in the cooled baked pastry shell and pour the custard over them.
Cool completely before serving.

recipes.title: Baked Custard
recipes.description: Simple old-fashioned milk custard with eggs and vanilla, baked gently in a water bath.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F) and butter a baking dish or several small heatproof moulds.
Beat the eggs, sugar, salt and vanilla together.
Scald the milk and add it very slowly to the eggs, stirring constantly.
Pour into the baking dish or moulds.
Set the dish in a pan of water and bake for 30-40 minutes, until a knife comes out clean.

recipes.title: Bread Pudding
recipes.description: Torn bread soaked in a sweet cinnamon custard with raisins and baked until set.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F).
Tear the bread into small pieces and put it in a baking dish, mixing in the raisins as you fill the dish.
Pour the melted butter over the bread.
Beat the eggs lightly, then add the sugar, milk, cinnamon and vanilla and mix.
Pour the mixture over the bread and press lightly so all the bread is wet.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Let cool and serve cold or warm, cut into squares.

recipes.title: Indian Pudding (Cornmeal)
recipes.description: Old New England baked pudding of cornmeal, milk and molasses with ginger and cinnamon; not an Indian dish.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F). Set aside 1/2 cup of the milk and bring the rest to the boil.
Stir the cold water into the cornmeal, then pour it slowly into the boiling milk and add the salt.
Boil for 15 minutes, stirring constantly, removing any skin. Take it off the heat.
Mix the molasses with the baking soda, the reserved 1/2 cup milk and the brown sugar.
Add the nutmeg, ginger, cinnamon and beaten egg yolks to the molasses mixture.
Pour the molasses mixture slowly into the cornmeal mixture.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold them in.
Pour into a greased baking dish and bake for 1 hour.

recipes.title: Baked Rice Pudding
recipes.description: Creamy oven-baked pudding of cooked rice, milk and eggs with raisins, cinnamon and nutmeg.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 165 °C (325 °F).
In a large 3-litre casserole dish, mix the milk, eggs and sugar until thoroughly mixed and frothy.
Mix in the cinnamon, nutmeg and vanilla.
Mix in the cooked rice, then scatter the raisins on top. Do not stir them in, or they will sink.
Set the casserole in a larger baking pan holding about 2.5 cm of water, to stop the bottom cooking too fast.
Bake until set, about 1.5 hours.

recipes.title: Lemon Squares
recipes.description: Shortbread base topped with a sweet-tart lemon custard layer, dusted with powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: powdered sugar, plus extra for dusting

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Combine the 2 cups flour and 3/4 cup powdered sugar.
Cut in the margarine until the mixture resembles fine crumbs.
Press firmly into a greased 8 or 9-inch square pan.
Bake the base for 20-30 minutes, until lightly browned.
Meanwhile, beat the eggs until frothy and stir in the lemon juice and lemon zest.
In another bowl, stir together the sugar, the 1/4 cup flour and the baking powder, then stir into the egg mixture until just moistened.
Spread over the hot base and bake for 20-25 minutes, until set.
Cool before cutting into squares. Dust with powdered sugar.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Roll
recipes.description: Spiced pumpkin sponge rolled around a sweet cream cheese filling, sliced and served for the holidays.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F). Line a rectangular cookie sheet with greased parchment, letting it overhang the sides.
Mix the sugar, eggs and pumpkin in a large bowl until well blended.
Mix the flour, salt, cinnamon and baking soda in a second bowl, then fold into the pumpkin mixture.
Pour the batter evenly onto the sheet, sprinkle with the pecans and bake for 15 minutes.
Set aside 2 tbsp of the powdered sugar. Whip the cream cheese, vanilla, butter and the rest of the powdered sugar until smooth.
Dust a clean dish towel with the reserved powdered sugar. Flip the warm cake onto it and roll up loosely. Cool completely.
Unroll the cake, spread the filling over it and roll it up again in a spiral.
Wrap in foil or plastic wrap and freeze. Cut into slices while still frozen.
